slot.subtopic: Diagonal relationship of Li and Mg
slot.brief: Ask which property is shared by Li and Mg but not by Li and other alkali metals (e.g. nitride formation / carbonate decomposition); match the diagonal-pair property.

stem: Which property is shared by lithium and magnesium but not by the other alkali metals?
options: Their carbonates are thermally stable toward oxide formation.
They form stable superoxides on reaction with oxygen.
They react directly with nitrogen to form nitrides.
Their hydroxides are highly soluble in water.

verdicts.working: Lithium and magnesium both react directly with nitrogen to form nitrides (Li₃N and Mg₃N₂); the other alkali metals do not. The remaining options do not describe both elements.

working:
$6\text{Li}+\text{N}_2\rightarrow2\text{Li}_3\text{N}$
$3\text{Mg}+\text{N}_2\rightarrow\text{Mg}_3\text{N}_2$
Among alkali metals, lithium is the one that directly forms a nitride with nitrogen.

Independent check: Lithium and magnesium both react directly with nitrogen to form nitrides (Li₃N and Mg₃N₂); the other alkali metals do not. The remaining options do not describe both elements.
solution:
Lithium and magnesium react directly with nitrogen to form nitrides:
$$6\text{Li}+\text{N}_2\rightarrow2\text{Li}_3\text{N},\qquad 3\text{Mg}+\text{N}_2\rightarrow\text{Mg}_3\text{N}_2$$
Among the alkali metals, only lithium shows this property.
